questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: BDE Enthalpy Calculation for H2 + Cl2
questions.question: Using standard BDEs (H-H: 436 kJ/mol, Cl-Cl: 243 kJ/mol, H-Cl: 432 kJ/mol), what is the calculated enthalpy of reaction (ΔH°rxn) for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2 HCl?
questions.explanation: ΔH°rxn = Σ(BDE bonds broken) - Σ(BDE bonds formed) = (436 + 243) - 2(432) = 679 - 864 = -185 kJ/mol.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Gibbs Free Energy and Equilibrium Constant
questions.question: At 298 K (25°C), if a reaction has ΔG° = -11.4 kJ/mol, what is the equilibrium constant Keq? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)
questions.explanation: Every ~5.7 kJ/mol of negative ΔG° at 298 K increases Keq by a factor of 10; ΔG° = -11.4 kJ/mol gives Keq = 10² = 100.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: For a cracking reaction with ΔH° = +80 kJ/mol and ΔS° = +200 J/mol·K, at what temperature does the reaction become exergonic (ΔG° < 0)?

options.label: D
options.text: The reaction is never exergonic at any temperature.

questions.explanation: Setting ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS° = 0 gives the crossover temperature T = ΔH°/ΔS° = 80,000 / 200 = 400 K.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: If Reaction A has Ea = 50 kJ/mol and Reaction B has Ea = 75 kJ/mol at 298 K, how much faster is Reaction A than Reaction B? (Assume equal A factors)

options.label: B
options.text: Both reactions proceed at identical rates.

options.label: D
options.text: Reaction A is approximately 24,000 times faster than Reaction B (k_A / k_B = e^(ΔEa / RT) = e^(25000 / 2478) ≈ e^10.09 ≈ 24,000).

questions.correct_answer: Reaction A is approximately 24,000 times faster than Reaction B (k_A / k_B = e^(ΔEa / RT) = e^(25000 / 2478) ≈ e^10.09 ≈ 24,000).
questions.explanation: A 25 kJ/mol reduction in activation energy at 25°C increases the reaction rate by e^(25000 / [8.314 × 298]) ≈ 2.4 × 10⁴ fold.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What value of the primary deuterium kinetic isotope effect (k_H / k_D) is diagnostic for rate-limiting C-H bond cleavage at 25°C?

options.label: D
options.text: k_H / k_D = 6.0 to 7.5 (due to the difference in zero-point vibrational energies between C-H and C-D bonds).

questions.correct_answer: k_H / k_D = 6.0 to 7.5 (due to the difference in zero-point vibrational energies between C-H and C-D bonds).
questions.explanation: The zero-point energy difference between C-H (ν ~ 2900 cm⁻¹) and C-D (ν ~ 2100 cm⁻¹) creates a theoretical maximum primary KIE of ~6.5–7.0 at 298 K.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Using BDEs (CH₃-H: 439 kJ/mol, Cl-Cl: 243 kJ/mol, CH₃-Cl: 351 kJ/mol, H-Cl: 432 kJ/mol), what is the calculated ΔH° for the net reaction CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl?

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: If a unimolecular SN1 ionization has a first-order rate constant k = 0.0231 s⁻¹ at 25°C, what is the half-life (t_1/2) of the reactant?
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, half-life is independent of initial concentration: t_1/2 = 0.693 / k = 0.693 / 0.0231 = 30.0 s.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What does an inverse secondary kinetic isotope effect (k_H / k_D ≈ 0.85 to 0.90) indicate about the hybridization change at carbon in the transition state?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-H bond.

options.label: C
options.text: An sp² (planar) to sp³ (tetrahedral) rehybridization during the rate-determining step, increasing steric crowding and out-of-plane bending frequencies.

options.label: D
options.text: An sp³ to sp² rehybridization with carbocation formation.

questions.correct_answer: An sp² (planar) to sp³ (tetrahedral) rehybridization during the rate-determining step, increasing steric crowding and out-of-plane bending frequencies.
questions.explanation: Rehybridizing from sp² to sp³ increases C-H/C-D out-of-plane bending force constants, favoring the heavier isotope (inverse secondary KIE < 1).

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Temperature Doubling Rule of Thumb Math
questions.question: Why does reaction rate roughly double for every 10°C increase in temperature around room temperature (25°C)?

options.label: A
options.text: Because the concentration of reactants doubles.

options.label: B
options.text: A 10 K rise increases the fraction of molecules possessing energy exceeding a typical activation barrier (Ea ~ 50 kJ/mol) by a factor of e^(Ea·ΔT / [R·T₁·T₂]) ≈ 2.0.

options.label: C
options.text: Because the activation energy drops to zero.

questions.correct_answer: A 10 K rise increases the fraction of molecules possessing energy exceeding a typical activation barrier (Ea ~ 50 kJ/mol) by a factor of e^(Ea·ΔT / [R·T₁·T₂]) ≈ 2.0.
questions.explanation: Applying the Arrhenius equation with typical Ea ≈ 50 kJ/mol gives k(308K)/k(298K) = e^([50000/8.314] × [10 / (298 × 308)]) = e^0.654 ≈ 1.92 ≈ 2.0.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Thermodynamic Equilibrium Ratio from Delta G
questions.question: At 298 K, if product B is 5.7 kJ/mol more stable than isomer A (ΔG° = -5.7 kJ/mol), what is the equilibrium ratio of [B]/[A]?
questions.explanation: At 298 K, ΔG° = -5.7 kJ/mol corresponds to Keq = 10¹ = 10, meaning [B]/[A] = 10:1 (90.9% B).

questions.question: What value of the primary deuterium kinetic isotope effect (k_H / k_D) is diagnostic for rate-limiting C-H bond cleavage at 25°C?

options.label: D
options.text: k_H / k_D = 6.0 to 7.5 (due to the difference in zero-point vibrational energies between C-H and C-D bonds).

questions.question: If a unimolecular SN1 ionization has a first-order rate constant k = 0.0231 s⁻¹ at 25°C, what is the half-life (t_1/2) of the reactant?
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, half-life is independent of initial concentration: t_1/2 = 0.693 / k = 0.693 / 0.0231 = 30.0 s.

questions.question: What does an inverse secondary kinetic isotope effect (k_H / k_D ≈ 0.85 to 0.90) indicate about the hybridization change at carbon in the transition state?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-H bond.

options.label: C
options.text: An sp² (planar) to sp³ (tetrahedral) rehybridization during the rate-determining step, increasing steric crowding and out-of-plane bending frequencies.

options.label: D
options.text: An sp³ to sp² rehybridization with carbocation formation.

questions.correct_answer: An sp² (planar) to sp³ (tetrahedral) rehybridization during the rate-determining step, increasing steric crowding and out-of-plane bending frequencies.
questions.explanation: Rehybridizing from sp² to sp³ increases C-H/C-D out-of-plane bending force constants, favoring the heavier isotope (inverse secondary KIE < 1).

questions.topic: Temperature Doubling Rule of Thumb Math
questions.question: Why does reaction rate roughly double for every 10°C increase in temperature around room temperature (25°C)?

options.label: B
options.text: Because the concentration of reactants doubles.

options.label: C
options.text: A 10 K rise increases the fraction of molecules possessing energy exceeding a typical activation barrier (Ea ~ 50 kJ/mol) by a factor of e^(Ea·ΔT / [R·T₁·T₂]) ≈ 2.0.

options.label: D
options.text: Because the activation energy drops to zero.

questions.correct_answer: A 10 K rise increases the fraction of molecules possessing energy exceeding a typical activation barrier (Ea ~ 50 kJ/mol) by a factor of e^(Ea·ΔT / [R·T₁·T₂]) ≈ 2.0.
questions.explanation: Applying the Arrhenius equation with typical Ea ≈ 50 kJ/mol gives k(308K)/k(298K) = e^([50000/8.314] × [10 / (298 × 308)]) = e^0.654 ≈ 1.92 ≈ 2.0.

questions.topic: Thermodynamic Equilibrium Ratio from Delta G
questions.question: At 298 K, if product B is 5.7 kJ/mol more stable than isomer A (ΔG° = -5.7 kJ/mol), what is the equilibrium ratio of [B]/[A]?
questions.explanation: At 298 K, ΔG° = -5.7 kJ/mol corresponds to Keq = 10¹ = 10, meaning [B]/[A] = 10:1 (90.9% B).
